name: Easy Strength (40-Day Program)
author: Dan John, Pavel Tsatsouline
structure: The same five exercises every day for forty sessions, never more than ten reps of any of them: two sets of five on most days, with days of 5-3-2, six singles or one set of ten mixed in.
progression: Load goes up only when it has come to feel light. No set is missed or ground out, and there is no deload.
adapt: The plan holds one layout, two sets of five, with progression off: the lifter raises a load when it feels light. The days of other rep schemes are not prescribed.
caveats: Fifteen to twenty minutes a session and easy to run beside a sport. It does almost nothing for size, and being that easy tempts people into adding load too soon.

name: Tactical Barbell — Operator
author: K. Black
structure: A cluster of two or three compound lifts trained every session for 3-5 sets each (1-3 for the deadlift), with at least two minutes' rest.
progression: A training max of 90 % of a one-rep max, with loads waving between 70 and 95 % of it over six weeks; then a retest, or a higher training max.
adapt: Loads are percentages of a training max that wave week by week; the app has no percentages and trains the same week until the plan is changed.
caveats: Never near failure, so it sits beside hard conditioning. Three or four lifts and no direct arm, shoulder or hamstring work. Only the outline was checked.

name: Power to the People
author: Pavel Tsatsouline
structure: A deadlift and one press, five days a week: a set of five at the working load and a second set of five at about 90 % of it.
progression: Start at about 70-80 % of a five-rep max and add 2.5 kg (5 lb) a session, in a straight line or in waves. No rep in doubt is attempted; when progress stops the cycle ends and a new one starts lighter.
adapt: A planned exercise has one load for all its sets, so the second set at 90 % is not prescribed. The wave and step cycles are the lifter's to run; the app's `linear` adds a step each session.
caveats: About 25 minutes a session, two lifts, little for size. Only its existence and outline are confirmed: the source is a forum summary of the book.

name: Minimum effective dose for strength
author: Androulakis-Korakakis and colleagues (2021)
structure: Each competition lift for about three to six sets a week of one to five reps, above 80 % of a max.
progression: Loaded by effort: sets finish at RPE 7.5-9.5. Singles at RPE 9-9.5 alone keep strength but may not add a meaningful amount.
adapt: The app does not choose loads from an effort rating. With progression off the lifter picks the load and logs the effort; `linear` with a small `inc` is the alternative.
caveats: A research finding more than a full programme: for a stretch when time is very short. Too little volume to live on. Only the outline was checked.

name: Jeff Nippard Essentials Program
author: Jeff Nippard
structure: Hypertrophy sessions of about 45 minutes, sold in versions for two to five days a week.
progression: RPE with double progression. A paid programme: its rules were not available to check.
adapt: Nothing beyond the product page is known about this programme, so its details cannot be laid out from here.
caveats: Paid. Only its existence and outline are confirmed.
